title: Who Saves the Labour?
paragraphs: Every wave of automation arrives with two confident stories. In one, machines will free people from drudgery; in the other, they will leave people with nothing to do. Both stories treat technology as the main actor and workers as an audience, which is precisely the assumption the historical record makes hardest to defend.

Consider the Luddites, the English textile workers who smashed machinery in the early nineteenth century. Their name now serves as shorthand for anyone who fears new technology, yet many historians argue that their grievance was less with machines as such than with the way machines were being used to cut wages and undermine skilled trades. Read that way, the protests were a dispute about who would capture the gains, not a refusal of progress.

Economists have since added a second complication. Machines rarely take over whole jobs; they take over tasks, and a job is a bundle of tasks. When automated teller machines spread across American banks, the number of human tellers did not collapse as many expected, partly because cheaper branches encouraged banks to open more of them and tellers shifted towards building relationships with customers. The example is often overused, but its point is sound: the effect of a technology depends on which tasks it replaces and which it makes more valuable.

None of this guarantees a happy ending. In nineteen thirty John Maynard Keynes warned of what he called technological unemployment, while suggesting that within a century people might need to work as little as fifteen hours a week. That shorter week has not arrived for most workers, and plausible explanations point as much to how the gains from productivity were shared as to anything engineers did or failed to do. Arguably, then, the decisive questions about automation are political before they are technical.

Treating workers as an audience, in other words, is not a neutral simplification. It quietly removes from view the very people whose bargaining power determines whether a labour-saving machine saves labour for them or merely saves on them.

questions.prompt: What is the author's central argument?

options.text: The speed of invention decides automation's outcome
options.explanation: Yazar soruların teknik olmadan önce siyasi olduğunu söyler.

options.text: Who gains from automation shapes its effects
options.explanation: Yazar kazanımların paylaşımının ve pazarlık gücünün sonucu belirlediğini savunur.
Metin veznedar örneğiyle bunun zorunlu olmadığını gösterir.

options.text: The Luddites simply feared new machines
options.explanation: Metin Ludditlerin şikayetinin makinelerin kullanım biçimiyle ilgili olduğunu söyler.

questions.prompt: Why, according to the third paragraph, did teller numbers not collapse?

options.text: Machines absorbed every task tellers once did
options.explanation: Veznedarlar müşteri ilişkilerine kaydı; tüm görevler makinelere devredilmedi.

options.text: Banks were legally barred from cutting tellers
Customers refused to use the new machines
Cheaper branches led banks to open more
options.explanation: Metin daha ucuz şubelerin bankaları daha fazla şube açmaya teşvik ettiğini söyler.

questions.prompt: In the final paragraph, what does a machine that “saves on them” do?

options.explanation: 'Save on' bir şeyden tasarruf etmek, kısmak demektir; yazar işçilere yapılan harcamanın kısılmasını kastediyor.
'Save' kurtarmak anlamına da gelir ama 'save on' bu anlamda değildir.
Bu, karşıtlığın öbür tarafı olan 'saves labour for them' anlamıdır.

To prove that automation creates jobs everywhere

options.text: To admit a weakness while keeping its point
options.explanation: Yazar örneğin sık tekrarlandığını kabul eder ama ana fikrini sağlam bulur.

sources.claim: Ludditler 19. yüzyılın başında İngiltere'de tekstil makinelerini parçalayan işçilerdi; şikayetleri ücretler ve vasıflı işin zayıflatılmasıyla ilişkilendirilir.

ABD'de ATM'ler yayıldıktan sonra veznedar istihdamı 1980-2010 arasında yaklaşık 500 binden 550 bine çıktı (işgücü payı düştü); ATM'ler şube işletme maliyetini düşürdü, şube başına veznedar sayısı 1988-2004'te üçte birden fazla azaldı ama kentsel şube sayısı %40'tan fazla arttı (kısmen bankacılık deregülasyonuyla da teşvik edildi); rutin nakit işleri azalırken veznedarlar 'ilişki bankacılığı' ve satışa yöneldi. Not: 'makinelerin kötü hallettiği işler' ifadesi kaynakta olmadığı için 'müşteri ilişkileri kurma' olarak yumuşatıldı. Autor örneğin paradigmatik alınmaması gerektiğini de belirtir.
